problem: The solution to the equation $3\operatorname{cos}⁡x-3=0$ for $\pi \le x<3\pi $ is $x=${{field-1}}.

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{cos}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =2 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the solutions to $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1$ correspond to the values of $x$ at which $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ attains its maximum value.

First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(1)={0}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${0}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={0}^{∘}.$

This solution is a quadrantal angle. To find the remaining solutions, we use our knowledge of the cosine function. We know that the cosine function has its maximum values at

$$
x={360}^{∘}\cdot n.
$$

Since the domain $-{180}^{∘}<x\le {180}^{∘}$ is one period, and we have already found one maximum value in this period, we conclude that $x={0}^{∘}$ is the only solution.
